task: Make Lattice the primary user-facing CLI command, document local/global rollout, and add a read-only rollout_check for cross-project validation.
outcome: User runs `lattice rollout_check --projects /Users/jek/Documents/Work/Orchestrate,/Users/jek/Documents/Work/plasmid --json` and sees `"overallStatus":"warn"` plus per-project `status` and `nextAction`; user runs `lattice story_create --help` and examples say `lattice ...` while `koala` is clearly described as a legacy alias.
facts: Global lattice and koala both resolve to Lattice CLI 0.3.5 after local npm install -g ./packages/main.
M1 real-project patrol showed Orchestrate passes doctor/check, while external projects can run lattice but often report managed asset drift through check.
Current help/session/doctor/check output still contains user-facing koala command recommendations even when invoked through lattice.
B-f3db established transcript-diff lifecycle evidence and verified global classifier/scope behavior locally.
Decision: deep koala-review-* lane IDs and .koala state paths remain historical authority identifiers; ordinary user command guidance migrates to lattice.
Decision: rollout_check MVP supports explicit --projects and optional --root discovery, both read-only by default.
constraints: Do not rename .koala state directories, signed artifact lanes, koala-review-* agent ids, or @koala-agent/core package identity in this story.
rollout_check must be read-only by default and must not apply managed assets or mutate scanned projects.
koala must remain a working legacy alias for old projects and historical scripts.
External projects may not contain packages/main or local node_modules; rollout output must degrade to WARN/SKIP rather than hard failing without context.
